cases.observed: The new-watchtower prompt produced an unfinished response repeating unrelated historical cliff operations and IDs; no Blender model was generated.
cases.verified_correction: Do not paste historic action payloads or old coordinates. Supply only short transferable lessons and use short stage-specific response schema.
cases.safe_lesson: Do not repeat old rejected actions or object IDs when starting a different asset. Use an original, concise plan for the current object.

cases.observed: Qwen returned syntactically complete creative JSON but supplied a shape primitive parameter object to the explicit-vertex mesh operation and selected architecture scales around 100 meters, creating nonexistent targets on retry.
cases.verified_correction: New assets begin with schema-constrained primitive objects and dimensions 0.15–8 in a small batch; later source-verified cycles can use full Blender mesh, UV, material, sculpt and nodes operations.
cases.safe_lesson: New assets need genuine, proportionate mesh objects before secondary details. Do not use nonexistent objects or substitute primitive arguments for indexed vertices.

cases.observed: Four genuine Qwen-directed Blender primitives exported as an editable BLEND/GLB; image revealed disconnected roof, overlapping masonry and several objects buried at wrong heights. The Qwen critique returned invalid JSON.
cases.verified_correction: Separate geometric sanity from visual certification; return invalid silhouettes to Qwen, require roof tiers, plausible contact and material/structural refinement on a verified existing source.
cases.safe_lesson: When creating an architecture asset, roof and shaft must occupy aligned, different real heights, parts must not be identical overlapping masses, and materials must be deliberately authored. Real Blender success is not art approval.

cases.observed: Real fixed-camera A/B of inherited timber watchtower shows roof and stair distortions from global landmark deformation, not a professional quality improvement.
cases.safe_lesson: For a small timber lookout mesh, do not deform the whole stair and roof assembly with broad landmark brushes. Choose local detail that preserves the existing architectural silhouette and connections.

cases.safe_lesson: Even when the local visual model self-critique sounds positive, compare real camera A-B and reject global deformations on a small inherited watchtower. Make deliberate localized changes and protect roof and stairs.

cases.observed: Genuine local artist Qwen proposed radius far below safe inspected source brush range on a combined wooden watchtower. Strict parser refused geometry before Blender. No output model produced.
cases.safe_lesson: For genuine inherited mesh edits, read actual source-relative brush limits and choose stroke distance and radius strictly inside both bounds. Never invent a smaller radius or repeat invalid brush decisions.

cases.observed: On actual Blender fixed-camera timber watchtower images, Qwen 8B named a cylinder RoofOverhang but placed it centrally at WORLD Z 3.27m (roof apex), so it produced a cropped roof-top disc, NOT an attached architectural eave. Positive executable outcome is not aesthetic improvement.
cases.safe_lesson: When adding a timber roof eave or overhang, ensure the ORIGINAL chosen geometry touches an actual X/Y outer roof edge and is below the highest WORLD Z apex; a central roof-top cylinder is not a realistic roof-edge detail. Check matched-camera A/B for visible and coherent improvement.
